output:
**What I found:** `src/lib/retry.ts` should go: delete it and switch on the `retry` option that `got` already has (the record calls this L4 CODE → L3 LIB). It's generic code that keeps breaking, and `got` is already installed and on the approved list. `isEligibleForDiscount` is not a bring-down candidate, because it's your own discount policy and the same team would still maintain it after the move.

**Why it matters:** Removing the wrapper gets rid of the code that caused both POST-retry incidents. By default, `got` doesn't retry POST requests. If you keep the wrapper, each new bug fix in it costs your team time for behavior that `got`'s maintainers already look after. Merging the three discount copies is still worth doing, but it's an ordinary refactor, not a move to an external capability.

**Do this first:**
1. Write down what `src/lib/retry.ts` actually does: attempt limit, which status and error codes it retries, delay curve, whether it honours `Retry-After`. Then set the same values as `retry` options on one shared `got.extend()` instance.
2. Move one real caller onto that instance and add a test that a failing POST is sent exactly once. Then move the rest of the callers and delete `retry.ts`.
3. Add an ESLint `no-restricted-imports` rule that blocks `src/lib/retry.ts` so it can't come back.

**What I did not check:**
- The repository files aren't in this workspace; a search for `package.json`, `src/lib/retry.ts` and `*discount*` found nothing. Everything below is based on your description. Run `rg -n "retry" src/` to confirm where the wrapper is used.
- `got`'s default retry methods (GET, PUT, HEAD, DELETE, OPTIONS, TRACE) are from memory, not checked against your installed version. Run `npm ls got` and read the `retry` section of the got 14 docs.
- I haven't confirmed that all three copies of `isEligibleForDiscount` are identical. Run `diff` on the three function bodies.

---

```
Scope:          Node.js 22 TypeScript API (single repo, one four-person team): src/lib/retry.ts; three copies of isEligibleForDiscount
Mode:           Assessment
Decision:       Bring down retry.ts to got 14 built-in retry (L4 CODE -> L3 LIB). No bring-down for isEligibleForDiscount; hand off.
Summary:        retry.ts is 140 lines of generic retry and backoff wrapped around calls that already go through got 14, with got's own
                retry switched off. It had six fixes last quarter, two of them after incidents where it retried non-idempotent POSTs.
                got excludes POST from retries by default, so using it removes the code and the cause of those incidents.
                The main risk is quietly changing retry behaviour (attempt count, status codes, delay); copy the current values into
                explicit got options before deleting. The discount function is domain policy staying with the same owner, so it is out of scope.

Candidates:
- src/lib/retry.ts (custom retry/backoff around outbound HTTP)
  - Move: L4 CODE -> L3 LIB (distance 1)
  - Landing: got 14 `retry` option (limit, methods, statusCodes, errorCodes, backoffLimit, noise, maxRetryAfter,
             calculateDelay) set on a shared `got.extend()` instance; hooks.beforeRetry for logging if needed
  - Owners: API team -> got maintainers (upstream); platform team owns approval
  - Evidence: 6 bug-fix commits last quarter; 2 production incidents from retrying non-idempotent POSTs;
              nothing domain-specific in the wrapper; got already in package.json and approved; built-in retry currently disabled
  - Variation: none reported. Any local quirks (custom codes, delay curve) fit in `retry.calculateDelay` or per-request
               overrides, so nothing blocks the move
  - Confidence: High (Medium until the default retry methods are checked against the installed got version)
  - Next action: write down current wrapper settings, set them in got options, migrate one caller, test that POST is not retried

Priorities:
1. src/lib/retry.ts
   - Why now: high churn (6 fixes/quarter) x high blast radius (production incidents, non-idempotent writes repeated)
   - Move: L4 CODE -> L3 LIB
   - Landing: got 14 `retry` option on a shared got.extend() client
   - Migration proof: one real outbound caller on the new client; test that a failing POST is sent once and a failing GET retries up to `limit`
   - Retire: delete src/lib/retry.ts and its tests once all callers are migrated; add a no-restricted-imports ban on the path

Gaps:
- The wrapper's real retry settings (codes, limit, delay, Retry-After handling) aren't documented; capture them before deleting so the switch doesn't change behaviour unnoticed
- If any POST endpoint really should be retried, it needs an idempotency key from the receiving service before adding POST to `retry.methods` for that call; never enable it globally
- Installed got version and defaults not checked in this workspace

Handoffs:
- isEligibleForDiscount (3 identical 40-line copies -> src/shared/discount.ts)
  - Reason excluded: same owner (same team, same repo) and domain-specific policy; this is an L4 CODE -> L4 CODE move,
    which bring-down does not make
  - Better skill: morphogenetic-architecture / architecture-guidelines to decide where src/shared/discount.ts lives
    (domain module vs generic "shared"), then architecture-as-code to ban local copies. The merge itself looks right:
    three identical copies of one policy will drift apart when the policy changes
```

The library and service surveys were skipped: `got` is already installed and approved, and nothing pointed to an external service.
